sources.title: Instagram chases YouTube with a push for longer, widescreen videos
Instagram Is Testing Ability to Share Videos up to 90 Minutes Long and Launches on Apple TV — but Unlike YouTube, It’s Still Not Going to Pay Creators

en.title: Instagram Tests 90‑Minute Video Feature
en.dek: Instagram is testing a new long‑form video format that allows uploads up to 90 minutes, with no current revenue‑sharing plan for creators.
facts: Instagram is testing a new format called "Features" that supports videos up to 90 minutes, according to The Verge.
Instagram is not yet offering a revenue‑sharing program for creators, according to Variety.
The new feature is currently being tested in the U.S. with a small group of creators, according to Instagram spokesperson Megan Buckley.
Creators can share clips of long videos as Reels to drive discovery, according to Variety.
Instagram plans to launch the feature on Apple TV, according to Variety.
body: Instagram announced a new long‑form video format called "Features", according to The Verge.
The format supports horizontal videos up to 90 minutes, according to the same source.
The announcement followed the launch of Instagram's TV app, which now runs on Google TV, Samsung TV, and Apple TV, according to The Verge.
Variety reported that Instagram is not yet offering a revenue‑sharing program for creators, according to the outlet.
An Instagram spokesperson said the platform is funding some creators directly, but a long‑term monetization model is not yet defined, according to Variety.
The spokesperson also said Instagram is exploring performance‑based incentives for creators, according to Variety.
The new Features are being tested in the U.S. with a small group of creators, according to Instagram spokesperson Megan Buckley, according to The Verge.
Creators can share clips of long videos as Reels to help people discover the content, according to Variety.
Instagram plans to add a remote‑control feature for playback on TVs, according to Variety.
Instagram wants to accommodate creators who tell stories in episodic series, according to Variety.
The platform also aims to keep Instagram focused on connecting friends, according to Adam Mosseri, according to both outlets.
The new long‑form format is part of Instagram's push to compete with YouTube, according to both outlets.
en.context: Instagram is expanding its video offerings to compete with YouTube, according to both outlets.
